model_organism.citation: Selective ablation of the androgen receptor in mouse sertoli cells affects sertoli cell maturation, barrier formation and cytoskeletal development (PMID: 21152390)
phenotypes: Altered Anxa9 transcript levels in Sertoli cells of SCARKO mice compared to controls
Anxa9 identified among genes related to cell adhesion and cytoskeletal dynamics with marked differences in expression
Context: defective Sertoli cell barrier formation, delayed barrier development, disturbances in Sertoli cell nuclear maturation, aberrant positioning of Sertoli cell nuclei and cytoskeletal elements

biological.citation: ANXA9 facilitates S100A4 and promotes breast cancer progression through modulating STAT3 pathway. (PMID: 38609357)
biological.summary: ANXA9 mediates S100A4 to regulate the AKT/mTOR/STAT3 pathway and participates in p53/Bcl-2 apoptosis in breast cancer. ANXA9 also transfers S100A4 into the tumor microenvironment and mediates cytokine excretion (IL-6, IL-8, CCL2, CCL5) to promote angiogenesis via self-phosphorylation at Ser2 and Thr69. In vivo, ANXA9 downregulation suppressed xenograft tumor growth and lung metastasis.

biological.citation: Annexin A9 promotes cell proliferation by regulating the Wnt signaling pathway in colorectal cancer. (PMID: 37349657)
biological.summary: ANXA9 expression is significantly elevated in CRC tissue and cells, and knockdown inhibits proliferation, invasion, and migration. Functional analysis revealed that ANXA9 co-expressed genes are enriched in the Wnt signaling pathway, and Wnt activation reversed the anti-proliferative effects of ANXA9 deletion. High ANXA9 expression correlates with shorter overall survival in CRC patients.

biological.citation: Targeting the ZMYM2-ANXA9 Axis with FLT3 Inhibitor G749 Overcomes Oxaliplatin Resistance in Colorectal Cancer. (PMID: 40427072)
biological.summary: ZMYM2 was identified as a transcriptional regulator of ANXA9, with ChIP-qPCR confirming ZMYM2 binding to the ANXA9 promoter, especially in oxaliplatin-resistant CRC cells. ANXA9 is significantly overexpressed in chemoresistant CRC tumors and oxaliplatin-resistant cell lines, and its knockdown reduces proliferation and enhances oxaliplatin sensitivity. The FLT3 inhibitor G749 suppresses ANXA9 expression in a dose-dependent manner and reduces tumor burden in CRC xenograft models.

biological.citation: miR-186-ANXA9 signaling inhibits tumorigenesis in breast cancer. (PMID: 37841425)
biological.summary: miR-186-5p directly targets ANXA9, validated by luciferase reporter assay, and there is a negative correlation between miR-186-5p and ANXA9 in human breast cancer clinical samples. Knockdown of ANXA9 mimicked miR-186-5p overexpression (inhibiting proliferation, inducing apoptosis), while reintroduction of ANXA9 rescued miR-186-5p-induced apoptosis in MDA-MB-231, MCF-7, and BT549 cells. The mechanism involves decreased Bcl-2 and increased p53 expression.

biological.citation: Annexin A9 promotes invasion and metastasis of colorectal cancer and predicts poor prognosis. (PMID: 29393380)
biological.summary: ANXA9 protein expression is significantly higher in CRC tissue than adjacent mucosa by immunohistochemistry, and is associated with invasion depth and lymphatic metastasis. ANXA9-positive patients show poor prognosis and ANXA9 is an independent risk factor for survival. ANXA9 siRNA knockdown in HCT116 cells decreased cell activity and metastatic capacity, downregulated ADAM17 and MMP9, and upregulated TIMP-1 and E-cadherin.

biological.citation: Exosome-derived ANXA9 functions as an oncogene in breast cancer. (PMID: 37294149)
biological.summary: ANXA9 is secreted by breast cancer tissue-derived exosomes and its expression is upregulated 1- to 7-fold in BCA cells treated with exosomes, but not in normal MCF10A cells. ANXA9 silencing reduced colony formation by ~30%, and decreased migration and invasion by ~65% and ~68%, respectively, in BCA cells. In a xenograft model, ANXA9 silencing reduced tumor size by nearly half, demonstrating its oncogenic role in breast cancer.

biological.citation: High Expression of Annexin A9 Promotes Cell Proliferation and Migration in Gastric Cancer via the TGF-β Signaling Pathway. (PMID: 34587407)
biological.summary: ANXA9 is overexpressed in gastric cancer cells and tissues compared to normal controls, and correlates with unfavorable prognosis. ANXA9 overexpression in HGC-27 cells increased migration and colony formation, altered cell cycle distribution (decreased G1, increased S and G2 phases), and modulated EMT-related proteins. Immunofluorescence showed ANXA9 mediates cell migration and growth through the TGF-β signaling pathway via SMAD2/3 and p-SMAD2/3.

biological.citation: Hsa-miR-105-1 Regulates Cisplatin-Resistance in Ovarian Carcinoma Cells by Targeting ANXA9. (PMID: 33680718)
biological.summary: ANXA9 is significantly upregulated in cisplatin-resistant ovarian carcinoma cells, while miR-105-1 is downregulated, and ANXA9 was validated as a direct target of miR-105-1 by luciferase reporter assay. miR-105-1 mimics inhibited ANXA9 expression and increased cisplatin sensitivity in resistant cells by upregulating P53, P21, and Bax and downregulating E2F1 and Bcl-2. Conversely, miR-105-1 inhibitor promoted ANXA9 expression and enhanced cisplatin resistance in sensitive cells.

biological.citation: Frequent Alteration of Annexin A9 and A10 in HPV-Negative Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinomas: Correlation with the Histopathological Differentiation Grade. (PMID: 30744186)
biological.summary: ANXA9 expression is downregulated in 42% of HPV-negative HNSCC tissue samples compared to normal epithelia. ANXA9 expression in tumors is significantly associated with oropharyngeal location and histological differentiation grade. These findings suggest ANXA9 may be implicated in the pathogenesis of HNSCC, in contrast to its upregulation seen in other cancers.

biological.citation: ERα and ERβ Homodimers in the Same Cellular Context Regulate Distinct Transcriptomes and Functions. (PMID: 35872983)
biological.summary: ERβ was found to bind to cis-regulatory chromatin of ANXA9 as a direct transcriptional target in MCF7 breast cancer cells, identified through RNA sequencing and chromatin binding analysis. ANXA9 was among ERβ-specific migration-related direct targets, suggesting it is regulated by estrogen signaling through ERβ. This identifies ANXA9 as part of the ERβ-specific transcriptome distinct from ERα-regulated genes.
